raw_response:
Well, let me think about this year same as every year. I'm old, I been doing this fifty years, my wife helps me but the kids all work in the city now. Five mu ain't much but it keeps us in grain and a little cash.

**Wheat first** — I'll plant after the maize comes off in October, like always. I use the same seed my neighbor Old Wang gets from the co-op, costs maybe 3 yuan a jin, I put down about 30 jin per mu. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer (that 15-15-15 stuff, 40 kg bag) across two mu, so about 20 kg per mu of the compound. Then when the wheat wakes up in spring and starts jointing, if it looks a bit yellow I topdress some urea, maybe half a bag per mu, that's about 20 kg. I water three times — once before winter to set it, once at green-up, once at grain filling. Each watering costs me 25 yuan or so with the electric pump. Spray herbicide in spring, that's about it. I don't mess with fungicide unless I see rust, and I ain't seen bad rust in years.

**Maize** — soon as the combine cuts the wheat in June, I get the neighbor boy with his tractor to plant maize right into the stubble, no tilling, no time for that. Denghai 605 seed, that's what everyone around here plants, one bag does about 3 mu. I put compound under at planting, maybe 15 kg per mu, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage, about 20 kg per mu. Usually the summer rains handle the water but if July gets dry I'll irrigate once. Spray for the borers and armyworm, one treatment.

I don't do nothing fancy. Same as last year, same as the year before. Last year wheat gave me about 400 kg per mu, maize about 450. Good enough. If I try something new and it fails, that's real money lost and at my age I can't take the risk.
